site._share_note: Optional, for link previews and icons (src/lib/shareMeta.js). description: the page's description and og:/twitter: text (escaped, so it may hold quotes). share_image: { src, width, height, alt }, the picture a link preview shows, relative to the site (made absolute with base_url); with it come og:image, og:site_name and a summary_large_image twitter card. icons: { ico, svg, png, png_sizes, apple_touch }, files relative to the site; without it the head keeps its one ./favicon.svg link, and the build puts that file beside the page: the site folder's own favicon.svg, copied, or with none a placeholder (one circle in accent, else theme.accent, else grey), said in the build's log. With icons set, the site's own icons are left untouched.
site.title: Example site
site.description: An example site built with post-pipe from two public feeds, ScienceDaily and ProPublica.

author.name: Example Author
author._note: Default author for local pieces that do not name one in their own frontmatter (ingest.js, src/adapters/LocalFolderAdapter.js, src/lib/byline.js). name (or display) is used when a piece has no author of its own; empty leaves unauthored pieces without an author.

timeOverlay._timeOverlay_note: The chronology stack: the panel headed Chronology down the left of the graph, months by week, that filters the graph to a span of time (src/components/TimeOverlay). show true (default) keeps it on the page as it always was; false builds the page without it, not hidden but left out, for a site where it takes more of the screen than it gives.

toolbar._position_note: Where the graph's controls sit. top (default since 2026-11-05): no bottom bar; they join the top bar after its pages and links, the view switch and the +, as icon buttons the height of the pills: undo, redo, Reset, a menu (an hourglass) with each dimension as a checkbox row (one on at a time), the readers layer's switch when readers have connected pieces, and the bucket size when the one on has it; the list of the tagz (a tag) when the graph draws tag nodes; and the sliders, which open the main view's panel, where the view actions are (Zoom to fit, Close all and Open all when there are containers, Unpin all, Reset sizes) and, when show.layout is on, the layout. The menu's heading is dimensions.groupLabel. The top bar then keeps to one row: when it does not fit, the source pills after the first shrink to their dot, then a page or link with an icon shows the icon alone, then the first pill's text gives way to an ellipsis. With a cover they are in the art state only when opening.topBarInArt is true, and there take no taps until the graph rests. bottom (the default before 2026-11-05): the bar along the bottom (undo, redo; the layout, cluster or ring; the dimensions; Reset; More, with the view actions); an embed without its source bar keeps the bottom bar either way. show: history, layout and dimensions each on unless set false.

tts._fallback_note: When the voice reading aloud fails (an engine's request errors, a browser voice errors or is not on the device), another voice reads on instead of reading stopping, said quietly: one line in the console and a small note under the voice picker, nothing over the text. voice-then-browser (default): another voice of the same engine (its default, else the next in the failing voice's language), then the browser's default voice, then the device's own. browser: straight to the browser's default, then the device's own. off: reading stops with the error, as before. Each voice is tried once; the first that speaks reads the rest of the chapter (src/lib/voiceFallback.js).

browser.label: Browser (Web Speech API)
browser._voices_note: Every voice the reader's device has is offered. The order: Google's voices first (Chrome brings its own, better than the system defaults), then these preferred names in this order (a device voice matches a name exactly or by prefix, so Samantha finds Samantha (Enhanced)), then every other voice; within each, voices in site.lang come first, then the rest alphabetically. The picker groups them by language. The default is the first voice in site.lang: a Google voice in Chrome, the first preferred voice the device has on a Mac. No cap unless maxVoices is set to a number; an embed caps the list at 5 unless it is set, and lists the voices without the language groups.
browser.cost: free — the device already has it, no key, no network

gemini.label: Google Gemini
gemini.cost: billed per character to whoever owns the key
gemini._exposed_note: Off in the picker on purpose. Turning this on bills a real account for every paragraph anyone reads. Set exposed true only for a build where the reader owns the key.

tts._note: available = the engine ships in the build and may be turned on. exposed = it appears in the reader's engine picker. An engine that costs the listener money, or needs a key they do not have, stays available and unexposed: present for whoever wants it, invisible to everyone who was handed this and should not be billed for reading.

theme.name: default
theme._colours_note: bg, surface, accent, text, text_bright, border, node_published, node_draft and tag_color: the page's colours, each a CSS colour. Any left unset takes the original dark look's (#1a1a2e, #0a0e1a, #64ffda, #a8b2d1, #ccd6f6, rgba(100, 255, 218, 0.2), #3498db, #7f8c8d, #f39c12), so a site that names none still gets an opaque reader (since 2026-11-07; before, an unset colour was written as undefined).
theme._mode_note: mode: light or dark, the site's default for a theme that has both (sketchbook); without it the device decides. A reader's own choice in the panel wins.
theme._name_note: default (the original dark look) or sketchbook (paper and pencil: warm off-white paper in light mode, graphite paper in dark, hand-drawn hulls, edges and card outlines, titles in a handwriting face shipped as fonts/NothingYouCouldDo-Regular.ttf with its SIL Open Font License). A viewer can choose the other theme, and the sketchbook's light or dark mode (else it follows the device), in the panel.
theme._timeOfDay_note: Off unless set. true, or { enabled, transitionSeconds (4), seasonTint (0.1), hemisphere ('north'), palettes: { <time>: { dark: [top, bottom], light: [top, bottom] } }, seasons: { winter, spring, summer, autumn }, text, quiet }. When a piece is selected or open, the page background fades to the palette for its scene.time_of_day (dawn, morning, midday, afternoon, dusk, evening, night, late-night), tinted by the season of scene.date. The default palettes keep text at WCAG AA in both modes. A piece's scene (time_of_day, date, place) is read from its text's front matter, else its frontmatter.json (scene object or top-level fields). The reader can turn it off in the panel.

cards._ledger_note: Every card gets one slug, discovered from what the piece already carries and never invented: a canonical the feed gives (canonical_url when it is not the item's own url, or a <link rel="canonical"> in its HTML), counted only when it is a web address (http or https, since 2026-11-05: a note in a piece's front matter where a canonical link would be is never read as one), else a DOI, else the slug part of its url's path (a number is fine: the path is the identity), and only with none of these a slug from the title (src/lib/cardSlug.js). Each item in feed.json carries slug and slugSource (canonical, doi, url or title). ledger (provisional): the file where the slugs are kept from one build to the next, relative to the site, cards.json by default, worth tracking in the site's git; a build adds the cards it does not hold, appends urls and titles newly seen for a known card, and never rewrites a slug, so a title that changes keeps its card. A new card whose slug is already another card's gets a plain suffix (-2, -3) on first sight, frozen too. Absent, the first build writes it. false keeps no ledger: slugs are discovered every build and not frozen. The slug merges nothing: one article arriving from two sources shows as two cards. Item ids are untouched.
cards._listen_note: Whether an open card (a tap on it, node.select) holds the listening controls under its title: play or pause, stop, and the voice and the speed, the same ones the reader's toolbar and the panel's Listening group have. There is one reading on the page: started in a card it goes on when the reader opens, and the reader's pause and stop act on it; a play elsewhere ends it. The sentence being read is marked in the card's text as it is in the reader. Default true; false leaves the controls out of the cards, and the reader's own stay. The graph's table (graph.bindings, docs/ACTIONS.md) can also put node.listen on a gesture.
cards._topicSlug_note: topicSlug (provisional): every item in feed.json also carries topicSlug, the literal best two words for what the card is about, beside its slug and never in place of it, so a card with a poetic title still says its subject plainly (src/lib/topicSlug.js, issue #39). The words are found where what the card says it is about (its subtitle, tags, topology and summary, or with none of the first three its title) meets what its text spends its words on, weighed against all the other cards of the build. A tag of several words that the text uses whole counts as one word of the pair, spelled as the tag spells it, so a topic slug may have more than two parts (negentropic-wu-wei); verbs and words that frame a claim (limitations, evidence) never win; and the two keep the order the card itself gives them. Nothing is frozen: a card's topic slug may change from one build to the next as the cards around it change, and it is kept in no ledger; slug, slugSource and cards.json are untouched. node tools/topic-slugs.js <feed.json> prints each card's topic slug with the four candidates that came closest, to judge the words by. Default true; false builds the items without it.
cards._topicSlugFoundTags_note: topicSlugFoundTags (provisional): how the topic slug reads the tags rosetta-tagz found on its own, the ones every reference of which says discovered (a phrase that recurs across its source's cards) or emergent (a concept the card's text matched), where neither the piece nor its feed wrote them. text (the default, Harold's choice of 2026-11-05) reads them as text: such a tag is no tag of the card's for its topic slug, takes no tag's weight and is never one whole word of the pair, and its words count only where the card's own title, summary or text holds them; so a card whose every tag was found is read like a card without tags, from its title, summary and opening. tags counts every tag as the card's own, as the topic slug did before. A tag the piece or its feed wrote (an explicit reference, or no reference at all on a site without rosetta-tagz) is the card's own either way, and so is a found tag the feed also wrote. The tags on the graph are untouched; this is only how the topic slug weighs them. For a site set to tags, give tools/topic-slugs.js --found-tags tags, so it reckons as the build did.

rtagz._note: This block turns on rosetta-tagz (rtagz for short), the project that finds and categorizes tags, a folder in post-pipe with its own programs (docs/POST-PIPE-USES-RTAGZ.md): off unless enabled is true. It merges the spellings each source uses for one concept, picks one label per concept, keeps every source's own spelling on the tag, and lets an item with no tags earn some from its text. engine: the folder holding rosetta-tagz's bin/, relative to post-pipe's root, not the site (default rosetta-tagz; absent, the build goes on with the tags as written). overrides: the site's human decisions in rosetta-tagz's overrides format, relative to the site (default rtagz-overrides.json; absent is fine). emerge (default true): items earn tags from their text against the concepts rtz-stone made. discover (default false): propose tags for a source with no tags of its own from phrases that recur across its items; three states: true attaches what it finds, "queue" (since 2026-11-04) finds the same and attaches none, writing the candidates instead to rtagz-queue.json beside the site's overrides file (each with its score, the cards it would tag and why it passed) for you to choose from, and false runs no discovery. To take a candidate from the queue, add its label to the overrides file's accept list (or run rosetta-tagz/bin/rtz-override accept <label> --file <overrides>) and rebuild: it is then attached to every card whose text holds it, in either state. A phrase holding a function word (onto, roughly, allowing) is never proposed, whatever its score; add words of your own to the overrides' ignore list. Whatever the state, a card that ends the build with no tags carries untaggedBecause (provisional), one line saying why, which the reader panel shows where the tag chips would be: source gave none, discovery off; source gave none, candidates queued (N); source gave none, nothing recurred; emerge found no concept; or, with emerge off, source gave none, every phrase refused. timeoutMs (default 120000): rtz-build is stopped after this long and the tags stay as written. rosetta-tagz never fails a build: any trouble is one logged line and raw tags.
rtagz._conceptSchemes_note: conceptSchemes: published vocabularies the site vendors as its own concept schemes, [{ id, path }], the path to a file in rosetta-tagz's vocab format relative to the site (fetched once by the site's owner with rosetta-tagz's own program; nothing is fetched at build). rosetta-tagz maps the concepts it finds onto them by label and by use; a mapping is a relation on a concept an item already carries, never a new tag. What rosetta-tagz reports comes through as it is: each mapping on its concept in the feed's _rtagz.concepts, each scheme in _rtagz.schemes with the licence rosetta-tagz gives it, and the vocabulary's own label on a tag reference whose concept matches it exactly. Empty or absent: no external scheme, nothing changes.
rtagz._ledger_note: ledger (provisional): the ids file, where rtz-stone keeps its concept ids from one build to the next, so a concept keeps its id, and the positions saved against it, when its spellings shift; a file relative to the site, rtagz-ids.json by default, written by rtz-stone and worth tracking in the site's git. Absent, the first build writes it.
rtagz._skos_note: skos (provisional): rosetta-tagz writes the site's vocabulary as SKOS, skos.jsonld and skos.ttl beside feed.json. { "base": an absolute IRI the concepts and schemes are named under (default urn:rosetta-tagz:, which names nothing on the web; a site that publishes its vocabulary might use its own address, such as https://example.org/skos/), "lang": the language tag on every label (default en; null for none) }. false writes no SKOS files. Absent: the defaults.

flow._presets_note: presets (provisional): the orders a reader can read the site's cards in, one after another, with the controls the reader already has. Each is a preset of Flow (flow/README.md), the part in post-pipe's folder that puts a site's cards in one order under a weight vector: the name of one in flow/presets/ (by-weight sorts the cards by score; by-neighbourhood walks from the newest card, each next card the heaviest among the nearest to the one before), or a path to the site's own preset, relative to the site. For each, the build runs Flow's programs over the finished feed (flow-select --all, flow-score --preset, flow-order) and writes the order into feed.json as flows (provisional): [{ name, description, mode, order }], order being the cards' item ids; the same feed gives the same orders. The reader's Next and Previous (the arrows and titles at the top and foot of the reader, the arrow keys, a swipe) then go to the neighbouring card in the order, passing over a card that cannot be read yet, a link card and the top bar's own pages; and the top bar's book (topBar.resume, when it names no start) opens a reader with no place yet at the order's first card, and anyone else where they were. With two or more, the main view's panel offers them as one row, Reading order (provisional), each choice a preset's name, with its description under the row; this device remembers the choice (the preference readingOrder, provisional), Reset the view goes back to the first, and changing it moves nothing in the graph. A preset that cannot be found, or a program that fails, is one line in the build's log and that order is left out. Absent or empty: no Flow runs, feed.json gains nothing, and Next and Previous follow sequence edges as before.
flow._next_note: next (provisional, default true): whether the reader's Next and Previous, the two arrows beside the text, the arrow keys and the swipes follow the reading order when presets are listed. false keeps them on sequence edges (a series' next part, as on a site without presets); the book still starts a reader with no place yet at the order's first card.

reader._note: How the reader pane presents a piece. Engine defaults keep the old reader.

header._note: kicker: an optional small line above the title, a list of parts joined with separator (default " — "). Tokens: {n} the piece's number, {n_words} it in words, {N_words} capitalized, {book} site.title, {author}, {title}. A part whose token has no value is left out. byline: "by <author>" under the title, default true, kept for the piece's author. A piece that names its authors shows them; one that names no one shows this site's author when it comes from the site's own folder, and no byline when it came in through another feed: the source's own pill, under the byline and date, names where it came from.

reader._progressBar_note: top (a bar along the top edge of the reader, default), side (down its right edge), or none.
reader._allowDownload_note: Whether the reader offers Export (download the piece as a markdown file). Default true.
reader._words_note: words (provisional): how much of the open card the reader shows at first. The reader shows one card at a time, nothing beneath it; Next and Previous sit above and below the text, and as two arrows at its sides that stay beside the text as it scrolls. 50, 100, 250 or 500: about that many words, to the end of the sentence that holds the last of them, with read the rest (provisional) under it to show the whole card in place. "whole": the whole card. "one" (one card at a time, offered from 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-11) still works and means "whole". Absent: 100. A visitor chooses for themselves in the reader's panel, Reading, Words before the next (provisional), and their choice wins on their device. A card opened at a paragraph or at a place partway through shows whole; so does the open card when the voice starts reading it.
reader._fonts_note: The faces offered for the text in the panel. default is the page's own face (Atkinson Hyperlegible) and is always offered. opendyslexic ships as fonts/OpenDyslexic-Regular.woff2, with its bold, italic and bold italic (OpenDyslexic-Bold.woff2, OpenDyslexic-Italic.otf, OpenDyslexic-BoldItalic.otf), next to the page, with its SIL Open Font License in fonts/OpenDyslexic-OFL.txt; it loads only when chosen.

graph._growCap_note: graph.growCap (default true): with zoomMode grow-in-place, a zoom in stops where two anchored containers would come within 16 px. false lets the reader zoom as far as they like (to the zoom's own limits); the containers then may grow into each other.
graph._note: Visual parameters for the graph. Here rather than in the code so they can be tuned without a rebuild, and so a fork can look different without editing components. Not all of these are exposed in the interface, and they do not need to be — being reachable is the point.

tag._show_note: Whether the tagz are drawn on the graph at all (src/lib/tagPills.js). true (default): every tag is drawn, as a dot or as its pill (labels), with every edge to it. false: no tag and no edge to one is drawn, and none takes a tap; the tag nodes stay in the layout and keep pulling, so every card sits where it would with them shown. The reader can turn them on or off in the panel (Show tagz on the graph), kept on this device; Reset the view goes back to this. With them hidden, a tag picked in the top bar's tag list still shows its pill, its edges to its cards, and the related tagz its lines go to, while it is picked.
tag._labels_note: Whether each tag shows its label, the pill, while show is true. true (default): every pill is drawn. false: each tag is a dot (markRadius) in its pill's colour and opacity, with every edge to it; hovering a dot shows its pill, with its forms, for as long as it is hovered, and a tag picked (a tap on it, or the top bar's tag list) shows its pill, and so do the related tagz its lines go to, while it is picked. Either way nothing moves: a dot keeps its pill's room in the layout. The reader can turn the labels on or off in the panel (Show their labels, under Show tagz on the graph, greyed while that is off), kept on this device; Reset the view goes back to this.
tag._markRadius_note: The radius of a tag's dot while the labels are hidden, in graph units, so it grows and shrinks with the zoom like everything else. Default 7. Round each dot a transparent circle of radius 22 (or the dot's own, when larger) takes a tap, so a finger can hit it.

timeAxis._dock_note: left | right | top | bottom. The axis is a ruler pinned to the edge of the viewport, not an object in the canvas: panning and zooming the corpus moves the corpus past it, the way a ruler stays put while the paper slides under it. A docked edge also decides the direction — a side rail runs earliest at the top, a top or bottom rail earliest at the left.

graph._edgeWeights_note: How strongly each link pulls in the cluster layout and how short it sits (src/lib/edgeWeight.js), with the degree and recency factors flow-score reads. mode: weighted (default, each link's strength and distance follow its effective weight) or uniform (one link distance and D3's default strength, as before). In weighted mode a link's effective weight is its own weight (capped at 1; 1 when absent or not above 0) times the symmetric degree factor 1 / sqrt(penalty(deg(source)) * penalty(deg(target))) over all non-containment edges in the feed, times the recency factor floor + (1 - floor) * x of the card end (the mean of both ends for card-to-card, 1 for tag-to-tag), times weights[layer] (for a reference edge, its type, such as person; 1 when not named). degreePenalty: none (n), sqrt (sqrt(n), default) or log (log(1 + n)). recencyClock: calendar (0.5 ^ ((newest - t) / day / recencyHalfLifeDays) from the newest dated card, 0 when undated, default) or session (1 - rank / (n - 1) in feed order). recencyHalfLifeDays: 365 by default. recencyFloor: 0.2 by default, so old or undated cards stay attached. distanceSpread: 1 by default; the strongest link in the force gets simulation.linkDistance (as the panel's Tightness sets it) and weaker links up to (1 + distanceSpread) times it (0 gives every link simulation.linkDistance). The reader can switch mode and degreePenalty in the panel (while toolbar.show.layout is on; degreePenalty in weighted mode). Non-default settings are part of the layout key. Relations between tagz (broader, related, closeMatch, broadMatch, relatedMatch, exactMatch) are never links in the force, so their weights change nothing in the layout yet.
graph._collapseGesture_note: tap (default) or doubletap: what opens and closes a container, on its title or its closed node, in the engine's own table of gestures (graph.bindings, docs/ACTIONS.md). A tap is under 4px of movement; more than that drags the container. With tap, a double-tap on a title zooms like anywhere else; with doubletap, it toggles the container instead and a single tap does nothing. A site's graph.bindings go over this.
graph._doubleTapMs_note: A single tap waits this long (ms) to be sure it is not the first of two, then runs what graph.bindings gives a tap there; two taps within it (and 32 px) run what they give a double tap, and neither single. By default a double-tap or double-click on the canvas, a hull or a title zooms in about 2x at that point and opens nothing, and on a card opens the reader; shift+double-click, or a double-tap with two fingers, zooms out.
graph._readablePx_note: graph.readablePx (default 16): the size, in CSS px on the screen, at which a card's title counts as readable: a card at it or over it is the target node.readable in graph.bindings, and node.zoomToReadable zooms in until the card's title renders at it.
graph._bindings_note: graph.bindings: which gesture on which target runs which of the graph's named actions, a list of { target, gesture, action } rows over the engine's own table. targets: container (a closed container or an open one's title), node (a card), node.readable (a card whose title already renders at graph.readablePx or more; without rows of its own it does what node does), space (the canvas). gestures: tap, doubletap, drag, longpress (graph.longPressMs, default 500). actions: none, container.toggle, view.zoomInStep, view.zoomAtPoint, node.zoomToReadable, node.openReader, node.select, node.listen, node.stopListening, node.move, node.resize, view.pan, view.deselect. A site row replaces the engine's rows for its target and gesture, and an action the site binds is bound only where the site binds it; an unknown action does nothing, with a console warning. Unset here, so this site has the engine's table: a tap toggles a container (graph.collapseGesture), selects a card and, on the canvas, deselects, a double tap opens a card's reader and zooms anywhere else, a drag moves a card or a container (or resizes a card from its edge) and pans the canvas. Every action, the defaults and an example table: docs/ACTIONS.md.
graph._layoutVersion_note: Part of the key the reader's saved positions are filed under, with the layout's name and the settings that shape it (the spiral's settings, the card size, the simulation, the containers' anchors and layouts, and edge weights other than the defaults). When any of those change, positions saved for the old arrangement are no longer read back and the layout places the nodes afresh; bump this to do the same on purpose. Old positions stay in the browser until the reader uses Forget. Positions a reader dragged are retired with the rest. Default 1.

spiral._mode_note: path (default): a container's chapters sit one after another on a golden spiral, radius growing by the golden ratio each quarter turn, so each next edge is short. scatter: the golden-angle arrangement. Containers of containers place their children beside the first one, the label about a third of the way down.
spiral._spacing_note: Gap between neighbouring cards along the spiral, in px.
spiral._startRadius_note: The spiral's radius at the first chapter. null = about two thirds of a card.
spiral._direction_note: outward (default): the first chapter sits under the container's label and the spiral winds clockwise outward from it, so the last chapter is on the outer end. inward: the same reading order turned round, so the first chapter is on the outer end, at the top where a new reader looks first, and the spiral winds clockwise inward to the last one beside the label.
spiral._anchorEnd_note: Which part of a container's spiral sits on its anchor (containers.<id>.anchor). center (default): the spiral's centre, its title there and the first chapter just under it. outer: the spiral's outer end, its last chapter, sits on the anchor, and the spiral is turned so the first chapter lies from it toward openTowards.
spiral._openTowards_note: With anchorEnd outer, the direction from the last chapter (on the anchor) to the first: down (default), down-left or down-right. Set per container under containers.<id>.spiral.
spiral._keepBelow_note: crown: no card and no part of the hull of an anchored container goes above the roots' crown, the line opening.crownY (a fraction of the cover art's height). Where the spiral would cross it, it is turned (the least turn that clears it, up to a quarter turn) or else moved down; nothing is cut off. null (default): no line.
spiral._cardScale_note: The scale a container's cards are drawn at, and spaced for, against graph.card (default 1). A card keeps its text at every scale; the reader zooms in to read it. Set per container under containers.<id>.spiral, with spacing, anchorEnd, openTowards and keepBelow, each over the graph-wide value.

graph._initialFocus_note: What the first screen frames: all (default) or a container id. A container is framed so its cards are still cards (initialFocusMinScale, default 0.4); when the whole top-level container fits at that scale, it is framed instead. Zoom to Fit always frames everything.
graph._visibleLayers_note: Which edge layers draw lines: sequence, authored, tag, topology, and reference (an item's references other than its tags; a reference type such as person draws those alone, and tag draws them too). Default sequence only. Containment is never a line; the hulls show it. A connected_to between two pieces that follow one another in a series is folded into that next edge.
graph._containerCount_note: Whether a container's title shows how many items it holds: the open container's label, the closed container's blob, and the source pill at the top. Default true.
graph._readingProgress_note: A thin bar along the bottom of each card shows how far this viewer has read it, filling as they go; a card read to the end keeps a full bar and a small tick. Kept in the viewer's own browser (viewState), never sent anywhere. Default true; false hides it.
graph._roots_note: true, or { seed }, to grow roots behind the graph: thin branching lines along the reading path, from the top container's title to each child's, to the first piece of each run and on along the sequence edges. A root reaching a piece draws in once the viewer opens it and thickens once they finish it (from their own reading progress). Seeded by seed, else the top container's id, so a book always grows the same roots. Drawn under the hulls, never takes a pointer; colour from --pp-root-color. Default false.
graph._containersStart_note: containersStart: closed or open, how containers start (and where Reset returns them). closed closes every container inside another (a book's acts; every container when none is inside another); open closes none. Unset: initialCollapsed decides ('all' or a list of container ids; none by default).
graph._links_note: Link nodes: an item whose front matter has link (or external_url, as JSON Feed items carry) and no body text. Its card shows its title, its subtitle (front matter subtitle) and its blurb (summary or blurb); a tap on the card, its corner arrow, or Enter follows the link, and the reader never opens for it. Its page (<id>.html) sends the visitor straight on. A JSON Feed item with external_url and no content is one too. newTab: external (default: a new tab for links off this site, the same tab for links on it), always or never. A site whose every item is a link node shows no reading groups in the panel (Reading, Paper, Listening).
graph._intro_note: A short text shown once under the title pill, on its own line in the top bar, for a site's bio line. A string is plain text (blank lines make paragraphs); { "text": "...", "format": "markdown" } is markdown, rendered when the site is built (links in it take taps). Off when empty.
graph._anchors_note: A container can rest on the cover's art: containers[<id>].anchor { x, y }, fractions of the art's width and height (settings.opening). With anchors and the cover on, the graph state rests at the home view (initialFocusMinScale, default 0.4, from the frame's corner) instead of the first framing, and a fresh layout, or Reset, puts each anchored container's centre (its title, or its closed node) on its anchor. Each anchored container keeps a frame of its own and stays pinned to its anchor: the anchor is its centre, closed or open, through every opening and closing, until the reader drags it; it then stays where it was dropped (kept across visits) until Reset. Zoom to Fit still frames everything. The anchors are part of the saved positions' key, so moving one retires positions saved against the old ones. containers[<id>].labelPosition: center (default, where the layout puts the title), top (centred at the top of the hull) or hidden (not drawn).
graph._initialScale_note: graph.initialScale { minCardWidthPx } (default 0, none): the first screen shows cards at least that many CSS px wide. With initialFocus a container, the first frame zooms in at least that far; when the container then does not fit, the frame is its top (a hanging container's anchor) and the rest runs off the bottom, for the reader to scroll and drag to. With anchors, it is the scale the graph state rests at (the larger of it and initialFocusMinScale), each anchor placed through it, so Reset comes back to it with every act on its anchor. Zoom to fit and the + and - keys zoom about the middle of the viewport, as before.
graph._containerLayout_note: How a container lays out its members: the golden spiral (default), or hang, chosen for every container by graph.containerLayout: "hang" or for one by containers[<id>].layout. A hanging container hangs from its anchor: the anchor is the top of its hull, and the members run below it in reading order as a chain at most hang.columns cards wide (default 2), each one card step from the one before, down the far side and back up the near side, so one end of the chain is low and the other at the top under the anchor. hang settings, in graph.hang for all or containers[<id>].hang for one: direction down (default; centred under the anchor, far side to the right), down-right or down-left (hung outward from the anchor, the hull's inner edge under it so nothing reaches back past it, for containers at the sides); firstAt bottom (default; the first member at the far, low end and the last at the top under the anchor) or top (the reverse); columns; gap (px between cards, default 12). The title sits in the far column's empty top when it fits there, scaled down to a card's width if need be, or else above the chain. The hull is the cards' outline padded by hull.padding (graph.hull.padding for all, containers[<id>].hull.padding for one; default half a card for a hanging container), and its top never rises above the anchor. Closed, the container is its pill centred on the anchor, drawn at graph.closedPillScale of its full size (default 1). containers[<id>].hull: false leaves a container's hull undrawn (a book whose acts and cover stand in for it); its title follows labelPosition as before. A container that holds containers is not hung; the containers in it are. All of these are part of the saved positions' key.
graph._zoomPivot_note: pointer (default): the wheel and a pinch zoom about the pointer and the fingers, the + and - keys and Zoom to fit about the middle of the viewport. art: every zoom (the wheel, a pinch, a double-tap, the keys, Zoom to fit, Reset's way back) is about one point on the cover's art, opening.zoomPivot, wherever the pointer is, so what sits round that point stays round it as the reader zooms in. A pan still moves the view. Without a cover, as pointer.
graph._nodePalettes_note: Node colours a reader can choose: [{ id, label, color, fillOpacity, labelColor }]. The palette in use colours every container, closed and open (its outline and its fill in color, the fill at fillOpacity, its labels in labelColor, else color; its label face stays its own, containers.<id>.labelFace), and the outlines of the cards inside containers (their text and reading bar keep their own colours). The first is used until a reader chooses another; with two or more, the main view's panel shows a node colour choice in its Look group (a swatch and the label for each), kept in this browser (viewState preference nodePalette) and cleared by Forget. Empty (default): the containers' own looks (_containerLook_note) and the cards' own colours.
graph._zoomMode_note: geometric (default): a zoom enlarges the whole graph as one picture about the zoom's point (graph.zoomPivot), so anchored containers move apart and off their anchors. grow-in-place: with anchored containers (containers.<id>.anchor on a cover), each one is drawn larger or smaller about its own centre, which stays where the graph rests it, on its anchor on the cover's art, at every zoom (closed: its node grows; open: its hull, cards and title grow about its anchor, an outer-end spiral's last chapter staying on it); they are not moved apart. The wheel, a pinch, a double-tap, the + and - keys, Zoom to fit (each container grown until the first meets the screen's edge) and Reset all zoom this way, about the point under graph.zoomPivot where it is drawn now, so a pan made before a zoom is kept, not scaled; a pan still moves everything, the containers off their anchors. A zoom in stops where two grown containers, closed or open, would come within 16 px of each other (their boxes, each grown about its centre); opening a container while zoomed in past that zooms back out to it. Dragging a grown container moves it with the pointer. Whatever is not anchored zooms as before.
graph._closedPill_note: The closed pill's look. shape soft (default): the engine's own soft rounded shape, the same every time for the same container; blob: an irregular rounded shape (eight corners round an ellipse, nearly straight sides, soft corners), kept for a site that wants it. status false leaves the container's status line off it. labelSize: its label in px at full size (before closedPillScale); null: 1.6 of card.labelMaxFontSize. Its colours and its label's face are the container's look (_containerLook_note).
graph._containerLook_note: A container's own look, per container under containers.<id>, drawn on its closed node and its open hull alike: fill, a colour, at fillOpacity (0 to 1; unset, as given); stroke, the outline's colour (none for no outline; unset, the container's own colour on the closed node and the containment entry's stroke on the open hull); labelFace, a family the site's fonts carry, for the closed node's label and the open hull's title alike (measured in it); labelColor, both labels' colour, drawn as given. The closed node keeps its glow in its outline's colour (none in the sketchbook theme). The containment entry's own colours (badgeColor, color) stay its chapters' cards'. Without these, the engine's own look, as before.

dimensions._groupLabel_note: What the group of dimensions is called where a reader sees it: the heading of the top bar's dimensions menu (the hourglass) and that button's name, or, with toolbar.position bottom, the label in the bottom bar and the heading in its More sheet. dimensions by default.
dimensions._labels_note: Rename any dimension wherever a reader sees it (the rows of the top bar's dimensions menu, or the bottom bar with toolbar.position bottom, and their tooltips): { "commits": "revisions" }, or { "commits": { "label": "revisions", "title": "..." } }. Ids: time, commits, narrative, chronology, and readers (the edge layer of readers’ connections, its own switch, off until turned on, shown only when there are any). Engine names unchanged by default.

_contributions_note: Readers' contributions, off unless a site sets "contributions": { ... }. Kept in their own file, never in feed.json or the text. src: the file, relative to the page (default ./contributions.json; copied from the site root when there). Each item: id, type (essay | comment | art | connection), author (a display name), created, status (only "approved" is shown), anchor { chapter (the piece's slug), and optionally exact, prefix, suffix: the passage it is about }, body (plain text, never HTML), title (an essay's), asset and alt (art: a png/jpg/webp/gif/avif path inside assetBase, default ./contributions/assets/), to (a connection's other chapter), test (true for test items). showTest (default false): show test items. Shown as a count on each card, a From readers section under the text, and connections as the readers dimension: a dashed edge layer, off until the reader turns it on. A passage that can't be found in the current text, or can't be told apart from a repeat, falls back to the chapter and says so. submit (default false): a form in that section to send one; endpoint (default ./api/contributions) is where it posts; limits { name 60, body 8000, exact 400 }.

opening._crownY_note: Where the roots' crown (the stem meeting the roots) is on the art, as a fraction of its height: the line graph.spiral.keepBelow crown keeps the anchored containers under. null: none.
opening._zoomPivot_note: { x, y }, fractions of the art: the fixed point of every zoom when graph.zoomPivot is art. null: none.
opening._fit_note: height (the default): the whole plant fits the screen's height in the art state. width: the plant (the art state's image above crownY) spans the screen's width, sideMargin px in from each edge, but never so large that the crown falls below the screen's foot (on a wide screen the plant is as large as keeps the crown on it); the roots run off the bottom and the rest of the art is reached by scrolling down into the graph state.
opening._returnAbove_note: crown: in the graph state a scroll up, or a drag down, anywhere above the roots' crown (the small plant, the title, the top bar) brings the art state back; below it the graph's own pan and zoom work as before. null: only at the top strip (grip).
opening._topBarInArt_note: The top bar (and its band, topBar.band) shows in the graph state alone, fading in over 200 ms as the page settles there; true keeps it in the art state too.

_opening_byline_note: byline.text is a same-tab link to byline.href. With a title over the cover it sits directly under the title in each state (under the art layout's last line in the art state, under the graph layout's one line at the crown in the graph state, moving between them with the page): its left edge at the last line's, its top gap (default 0.3) of the title's size below that line's baseline, in the title's face and colour, at size (default 0.25) of the title's size (its largest span), never under minSize px (default 0, no floor), at opacity.art (default 0.35) in the art state and opacity.graph (default 0.56) in the graph state (a single number for both). It stays a link in both states. case: lower (default) draws it in lower case, as-written as written. graphScale (0 to 1; default null): in the graph state the byline is that share of the graph layout's title size (its largest span), never set to a line's width there (title.fit), and its gap is of that size too; it moves between its art state size and this as the page moves; null: as in the art state. Without a title it sits centred under the art and fades out as the page moves to the graph, as before.
_opening_title_note: Optional: a title set over the cover, as text. art and graph are its two layouts, crossfaded with the images: lines, each { x, y, spans }, with x the line's left edge and y its baseline as fractions of the canvas's width and height, and spans, each { text, size, rise }, with size and rise (a lift off the baseline) as fractions of the canvas's width, so the title scales and moves with the art. font names a face (a site's own in fonts, below), followed by 'Arial Black', Impact, sans-serif; color defaults to the accent; opacity is the text's. text is its accessible name (default: the art layout's words). hideGraphTitle (default true) leaves the graph's own title for the whole book undrawn while the cover carries it.
_opening_backdrop_note: How strongly the art shows behind the graph. backdrop.opacity (0..1, default 1) is the graph state's roots at the zoom the graph rests at; zooming in they fade toward opacityZoomedIn (default 0.3), reached at zoomForFloor (default 2.5) times that zoom and held further in; zooming back out they return. keepAbove (a share of the canvas's height from the top, default 0) is the part of the graph state's image that keeps its own strength whatever the zoom, such as a small plant above the roots: it is drawn as a second copy of the image masked to that part, with a short soft seam. The earlier graph.artOpacity is still read as backdrop.opacity.
_opening_reach_note: Off by default. reach.enabled draws rootlets from the art to the containers: thin, seeded, forking lines in screen space, in one layer between the art and the graph. tips: points on the art, each { x, y } as fractions of its width and height (the root ends the rootlets grow from). Each container they reach for (those with an anchor, else each child of a top-level container) is reached from its perContainer nearest tips (default 3); a rootlet is aimed at the container's centre and stops stopShort px (default 18) before its outline, closed or open. When a container is dragged or the graph pans or zooms, the ends re-aim, easing over lagMs (default 600); the starts stay on the art. A rootlet draws in over drawMs (default 1800) the first time it shows. They fade with the backdrop's roots as the graph is zoomed in. Reduced motion: they appear without drawing in and follow at once. Anchors: containers[<id>].anchor { x, y }, fractions of the art, rests a container there in the graph state (see graph._anchors_note).
_fonts_note: A site's own faces: [{ family, file, license }], file and license relative to the site root (ttf, otf, woff or woff2). Copied next to the page, declared with @font-face and preloaded; nothing is fetched from elsewhere. A face whose file is missing is left out with a warning, and text set in it falls back.
_accent_note: Optional: one accent colour for the site in every theme (links, the reader's and the panel's accent, the top bar's open control, its menu's checks and the view in force, the bottom bar's active pill in the sketchbook theme, the selected state). Kept as given wherever it reaches WCAG AA (4.5:1) for text, else moved toward black on paper or white on graphite just far enough; the tint behind an active control is the colour at 12%. Empty: each theme keeps its own.
_views_note: The views the site offers, by id from the engine's registry (src/views/index.js): cluster (the graph drawn with the cluster layout) and ring (the graph drawn with the ring layout); more may come (vision/VIEWS.md). The first is the default. With more than one, the top bar shows a switch, one plain button per view in the pill style after the pages and links, and ?view=<id> in the address picks one; the reader's choice is remembered on the device, and Reset puts the first back. The layout picker (the Layout row in the main view's panel, and the bottom bar's with toolbar.position bottom) keeps working beside it: picking ring there is the ring view. An unknown id is skipped, said in one line in the page's console. Absent or empty: ["cluster"], no switch, the page as it was.

resume.label: read where you left off
resume.icon: <g fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2"><path d="M12 7v14"/><path d="M3 18a1 1 0 0 1-1-1V4a1 1 0 0 1 1-1h5a4 4 0 0 1 4 4 4 4 0 0 1 4-4h5a1 1 0 0 1 1 1v13a1 1 0 0 1-1 1h-6a3 3 0 0 0-3 3 3 3 0 0 0-3-3z"/></g>

_topBar_resume_note: The book here: topBar.resume with Lucide's book-open icon and its label as its name, and no start, so a reader with no place yet starts at the first card of the reading order in force (flow.presets; by-weight's until the panel's Reading order says otherwise), and anyone who has read here goes back where they were. The label is provisional on this site.
_topBar_staleAge_note: A feed whose fetch failed when the site was built shows its cards from a copy: the newer, by fetchedAt, of the engine's last good copy (kept by every good fetch in the engine's .feed-cache/last-good/, on the machine that builds) and the site's saved copy (the file its outline's savedCopy names in feeds.opml, shipped with the site; see README.md), and its source in feed.json says so (stale, copyDate, copyFrom: site or engine, error); with neither it has no cards and its pill is struck through, as before. A stale feed's pill shows a small ringed ! after its count, and its popover says why, which copy and how old it is. staleAge (default false): true also shows the copy's age inside the mark (! 2d), to be read at a glance without the popover.
_topBar_sourcePopover_note: Every source pill with a date to show has a small popover just below it (a folder's pill, with topBar.groupByFolder, has none), shown while a mouse rests on the pill (not its dot), while the keyboard's focus is on it, and after a finger's dwell on it (a press held about 500 ms without moving) until a few seconds after the finger lifts; the mouse leaving, blur, Escape and a tap elsewhere put it away. A tap still hides or shows the source and a dwell does not; the dot keeps its own hover and tap, which open its colour ring. It says, in the reader's own locale and time zone, when the source's items were taken in: Fetched <date, time>, <age> ago for a feed (fetchedAt on its source in feed.json), and The feed says it was updated <date, time> when the feed gives a date for itself (feedUpdated: RSS lastBuildDate, else the channel's pubDate, else its dc:date; Atom's updated; JSON Feed gives none); Read at build <date, time> for a local folder, a page or a list of pages (readAt, or a page's fetchedAt); for a stale or failed feed, what is said above. The pill's title says only what a tap does, and its aria-describedby names the popover, so a screen reader reads it with the pill. Nothing to set.
_topBar_note: The top bar, in line with the source pills and the settings (the gear, or, with toolbar.position top, the sliders among the graph's controls), in the graph state of a cover, and in its art state too with opening.topBarInArt true. pages: [{ id, label, hideFromGraph }], a button each after the pills that opens that item in the reader; id is the item's id or its slug (the last part of its url, without .html); label is the button's text. hideFromGraph: true takes the item out of the graph (its node and every edge to it), so the button is the way to it. icon (optional): an SVG body string on a 24-unit box (the markup inside <svg>, e.g. an Iconify body), drawn in the button at the pills' height; showLabel (default true) shows the label as text beside it, false the icon alone (the label stays its name). links: [{ id, label, href, icon, newTab, showLabel }], a button each after the pages that goes to href (the same tab, or a new one with newTab: true, rel noopener; http, https, mailto or a path on the site), showing icon with label as its accessible name and title, and label as text too when showLabel is true (default false; a link without an icon always shows it). When the row does not fit on one line (with toolbar.position top), a page or link with an icon shows the icon alone. subscribe: { action, method, field, label, icon, placeholder, thanks, error, newTab }, an email sign-up, off unless action is set (a path on the site such as /api/subscribe, or an https address): an icon button after the links (icon, else label as text; label its accessible name) opens a small sheet under the bar (a dialog; Escape or a tap outside closes it, the focus goes to the field) with one email field (placeholder), a submit button reading label, and a message line. A submit posts JSON { [field, default email]: the address } to action with method (default POST) and Content-Type application/json; on a 2xx reply the sheet shows thanks and clears the field, otherwise the reply's own error (a JSON { error }) if it has one, else error, and error when the request fails. The sign-up sends nothing until a reader submits, and then only to the address the site set; nothing is sent on load. newTab: true sends the form the plain way instead (form-encoded, into a new tab), for a service with its own page. addFeed (default true): the + after the pills, for adding a feed, or, when the pasted address is a page naming no feed, that one page (a type="page" entry in feeds.opml); false leaves it out. autodiscover (default true): the + fetches the pasted address, from the reader's browser, to find the feed it names or to recognise a page; false takes the address as written and fetches nothing. showSourcePills (default true): false leaves out the source pills. groupByFolder (default false): true puts a pill for each folder of feeds.opml (an outline holding outlines) before its sources, which hides or shows them all. resume: { label (default read), icon, showLabel, start }, a button that opens the reader where this reader was (the item read most recently), else at start (an item id or slug), else, when the site lists Flow presets (flow.presets), at the first card of the reading order this reader chose that can be read, else at the first item; the top bar's own pages and link cards never count. order: the buttons' order by id (resume, a page's or a link's id, subscribe); any left out follow in the default order (resume, pages, links, subscribe).
_opening_graph_note: opening.graph.artStateOpacity (default 0.6): in the art state the graph hangs from the roots where it rests in the graph state (it moves with the art, so anchored containers stay at their anchors), at this strength, and comes up to full strength as the page moves to the graph; at 0 it is not drawn in the art state at all. opening.graph.hiddenUntilMove (default false): true leaves the graph (the hulls and pills) and the rootlets undrawn, on a load that starts on the art, until the reader first moves (a scroll or swipe down, a drag, or a tap anywhere but a top-bar control); they then fade in and stay. The top bar is in the art state only with topBarInArt true; there its pills, pages and links take taps, and the graph's controls in it take none until the graph rests. With toolbar.position bottom, the bottom bar fades in with the graph state.
_opening_grip_note: opening.grip.extra (default 16): in the graph state the grip that brings the cover back is the whole top strip, full width, from the screen's top down to the bottom of the top bar's row (the source pills, the pages, the controls in line with them, and the gear; not the intro under them) and this many px below it. The controls in the bar stay on top and keep their taps; a tap in the gaps between them, or a drag down from there (touch or mouse), brings the cover back. The grip's mark stays at the top centre as the hint.
_opening_top_note: opening.top: { art, graph }, px of space between the page's top controls (the source pills, the top bar's pages and the settings gear; the screen's top without them) and the plant's top edge, in the art state and the graph state. Where the plant starts in each state image is read off the image itself (its first row with ink). With art set the art state's art is as large as fits from there down (not centred); with graph set the graph state's plant sits there and graph.artOffset is not used. Unset (default): the art state centres the whole canvas and the graph state scrolls it up by graph.artOffset.
_opening_note: A cover as the page's top state, off by default. mode two-state (the only one): the cover art fixed behind the page, and the graph drawn over it. art: artState and graphState, two images of one canvas (the same size, the parts they share in the same place), stacked and crossfaded as the page moves, the art state's at 1 - p and the graph state's at p; or full alone, one image for both states; paths relative to the site root. In the art state the whole canvas fits the screen with byline.text under it (a same-tab link to byline.href); in the graph state it is scrolled up by graph.artOffset of its height (0.33 puts the place where the plant meets the roots about a quarter of the way down a phone) with its roots at backdrop.opacity (see _opening_backdrop_note), and the graph, hanging from the roots in both states (see _opening_graph_note), comes up to full strength over it (with toolbar.position bottom, its bottom bar fades in with it). The art never pans or zooms with the graph. Scroll, a touch drag, a tap on the art, or ArrowDown, PageDown or Space go to the graph; ArrowUp or PageUp, a scroll up at the top edge, or the grip (the top strip, see _opening_grip_note) go back; a reader can scrub partway and it settles at one of the two over snapMs. alt describes the image. ground: dark (default) puts the art on the theme's dark paper and keeps the page in dark mode, the reader and the panel keeping the reader's own mode; paper puts it on the theme's paper; or an object for a night sky (a dark ground): { top, bottom, textureFrom, colorFrom, texture } — the base colour is top (default #050505) down to colorFrom (a share of the screen's height, textureFrom unless set) and runs to bottom at the foot (empty: the theme's dark paper); the paper's grain and fibres are absent above textureFrom (default 0.35) and come in toward the foot, the ground adding its own copy at texture strength (default 1, 0 for none) so they are stronger low. startOn: remembered (where this reader left it, the art for a new reader; Forget clears it), art or graph. A #read= link opens on the graph. Reduced motion: the two states swap in a short fade, with no scrolling.
_opening_title_fit_note: opening.title.fit width: each line that names a width (line.width, a fraction of the art's width) is set to that width once the title's face has loaded, its spans scaled together, and the byline is set to the width of the layout's last line, under it in each state.
_opening_graph_rootsFit_note: opening.graph.rootsFit width: in the graph state the art is scaled so the roots' widest row (below crownY on the graph state's image) spans the screen's width, or, on a wide screen, so the graph state's image from its small plant to its foot fits the height. The art moves and scales between the two states. With artStateOpacity 0 the graph is not drawn at all in the art state (display none, nothing to hit).
_topBar_band_note: topBar.band: { color }, a band the screen's width behind the top bar, from the screen's top to 8 px under the bar's row, drawn by the two-state cover (opening) and coming and going with the bar. null: none.
_opening_rootsVector_note: opening.art.rootsVector: an SVG of the graph state image's roots (one path per part of each edge of the roots' tree, as src/lib/rootsVector.js reads it: data-e, data-part, data-a, data-b, data-tip, data-loop, data-free, stroke, stroke-width; and circle data-tip for each tip), drawn in the graph state in place of the image's roots below backdrop.keepAbove. Each act's roots (containers.<id>.rootTips, tip names from the file; or else the tip nearest its anchor) bend toward it when it is moved: the last third of each root, eased in, its tip by the whole move, what grows off it moving with it. The rootlets (opening.reach) are not drawn for an act that has such roots. Empty: the image's roots.
_rights_note: settings.rights { holder, year, statement, noAiTraining, position }: one quiet line, © year holder and the statement, on the graph page, under the reader's text and on every piece's own page, with copyright (and noai) meta tags. position: unset, the graph page's line sits above where a bottom bar would be (58 px up); bottom-edge, at the screen's very foot: its last line's baseline 6 px above the bottom and the safe area, no margin beyond that, 11 px on a wide screen (one line) and 10 px on a phone (at most two lines, set a little narrower to fit), in the quiet text colour, taking no taps but on a link in it; it lies over the picture (the cover keeps no room for it) and fades to a quarter while a card is under it.
_opening_graph_rootsBrightness_note: opening.graph.rootsBrightness (0 to 2, default 1): the roots' brightness in the graph state (the graph state image's roots below backdrop.keepAbove, and the vector roots, art.rootsVector), as a CSS brightness(): below 1 darker, so what the graph draws over them stands out. The art state keeps its roots as drawn; the two crossfade as the page moves. The small plant above keepAbove is not touched.
_opening_graph_footRoom_note: opening.graph.footRoom (px, default 0): with graph.rootsFit width on a wide screen, where the graph state's picture is fitted to the height, this much is kept free under its foot (besides the rights line's room, if it keeps any), for what hangs below the roots' ends, such as a closed act on the lowest tip. A phone, fitted to its width, is not changed.
_opening_rootsFollowMs_note: opening.art.rootsFollowMs (default 0): how far behind its act each act's vector roots follow it, in ms. The bend is driven by where the act is drawn on the screen at each frame (a closed act part way through any move it is easing over, an open one where its cards are), never by where it is going or by the pointer, and follows it as a critically damped spring with this time constant (it covers about 60% of a jump in that time and 95% in 2.4 times it, never overshooting), so the act moves first and its roots answer: when it is dragged, opened, closed, pushed clear of another, sent back by Reset, or zoomed. 0: the roots are where the act is drawn, at once. Reduced motion: at once.
